# Optional historical remote cleanup only; never used for new extraction.

AmuseMe turns a PDF (a research paper, a medical letter, a court opinion, a class handout or a business brief) into a reading guide where every explanation cites an exact quote. Choose a guided walkthrough, its main claims and limits, or a document map, then open any quote highlighted in the clean text or beside the original page. Read the complete document and download its text, images and processing report.

1. **Upload a PDF.** Choose how you want to read while AmuseMe processes the document. Live progress says in plain words what Muse is doing ("Muse is checking page 2 of 4"), lists every stage and shows the time elapsed. A short document takes about five minutes; a document too long for one run gets a clear message instead of a technical error.
2. **Choose a way in.** Read a short overview, follow a walkthrough, or examine the main claims, their support and their limits. Each AI-written explanation links to quotations in the uploaded paper. A document map shows which passages each step and claim cites. Older saved documents without a guide remain available in the normal reader.
3. **Check the document.** Open the quoted passage highlighted in its page text, or switch to the original page. Browse the full text, equations, tables and figures. The processing report says what Muse double-checked: problems a second review fixed, and places where Muse kept the original text. AI explanations and figure descriptions remain separate from the source.
4. **Take it with you.** Copy the complete normalized text or download a ZIP. The structured document includes its saved guide; the processing report records changes and unresolved issues.

**Meta Muse Spark 1.3 performs every runtime model stage, including initial extraction.** Local PyMuPDF renders source pages and crops proposed figure regions. Crops carry their source-page provenance; they are not labeled native embedded images.
| Page extraction | Transcribe each physical page into ordered text, tables, equations and figure regions | High |
| Reading guide | Explain the document and its main claims with exact quotations from its source blocks | High |

The earlier MinerU-plus-Meta workflow processed all six pages of Guo et al.'s *MFGLib: A Library for Mean-Field Games* (JOSS, 2026; CC BY 4.0). Page 3 was rasterized to exercise extraction from a scanned equation and code page.

That historical run does not verify the new Meta-only extraction path. The benefit demonstrated on this paper was that useful figure context reaches a reader that only receives text. It is one example, not a general accuracy benchmark. The output still contained imperfect code formatting and bibliography punctuation.
| `document.json` | Structured document with source locations and the saved reading guide, when generated |

New processing is disabled by default. To enable it, configure `META_API_KEY`, an authorized processing budget, and a stable budget ID in `.env.local`, then set `AMUSEME_PROCESSING_ENABLED=true`. Processing sends document evidence to Meta and can incur charges. Keep the same budget ID and data directory across restarts so spending records remain intact. Historical MinerU outputs and notices remain preserved.

The [experimental Spark extraction command](cli/spark-extraction/README.md) runs a bounded, single-page trial through the existing normalization and export workflow. Its guide covers prerequisites, local inspection and explicitly authorized execution; normal uploads use the multipage version-2 Meta extraction path.

Upload admission allows English-language PDFs up to **50 MiB and 50 pages**, with additional document complexity, model context and spending limits. Mandatory stage reservations are checked against the document cap before any model call. With the current $30 per-document cap and stage reservations, seven or more pages exceed that allowance even before figure descriptions. The application runs locally on a single host and retains documents for seven days.

Historical extraction experiments used MinerU; their [MinerU and service dependency notices](modal/amuseme_mineru/NOTICE.md) remain included. PDF validation and page rendering use PyMuPDF; its [license notices](python/README.md#provenance-and-licenses) are included.

Use the pinned Node 24.19.0, pnpm 10.33.0, installed application dependencies, and the existing Python 3.14 / PyMuPDF 1.28.2 runtime. Run from the repository root after `pnpm check`, `pnpm test`, and `pnpm build`. Preserve the original private environment, data directory, and budget ledger. The environment must identify budget `amuseme-authorized-2026-10-27` with its original $37 processing ceiling. The command reserves at most $5.50 for extraction, page checking, and heading restoration. Normal uploads use multipage Meta extraction version 2; this command retains the historical version-1 contract.

This runbook describes the current single-host application. It binds **127.0.0.1 only** and accepts a canonical `http://127.0.0.1:<port>` or `http://localhost:<port>` origin with the same port. It is not a public deployment guide. Normal model processing is Meta-only. Historical MinerU service operations remain in the [MinerU/Modal runbook](mineru-modal.md).

| `META_API_KEY` | Required for all current model stages. Never print the credential. MinerU settings are not required for processing. |
| `AMUSEME_MINERU_URL`, `AMUSEME_MINERU_TOKEN` | Optional historical remote cleanup only. Retain existing configuration when preserving a saved document policy; do not substitute other applications’ resources. No new extraction or saved-job retrieval is dispatched through MinerU. |

Run the test/build commands in the candidate checkout before replacing a serving build. Verify the affected flow in Chrome through CUA accessibility/native controls or supported Chrome DevTools commands, or in the cmux built-in browser (WebKit) when Chrome cannot be driven. Playwright is prohibited; use the [manual verification harness](development-harness.md#verify-in-a-browser). Browser checks do not authorize real processing. For development, `pnpm dev` builds and watches the guarded server, while `pnpm dev:app` rebuilds the UI. Provision invited `user` or `admin` accounts with the existing `pnpm provision:user` command and private `AMUSEME_INVITE_*` configuration from [.env.example](../../.env.example); public signup is disabled.

Historical MinerU retrieval was authenticated **GET `/jobs/{saved-attempt-UUID}`** at the configured gateway. The retained historical adapter owns this lookup and bounded polling; the current Meta-only runtime refuses its dispatch and retrieval. Use the saved extraction UUID; do not create a new UUID or repeat POST to “recover.” A completed archive settles the same receipt. GET 404/503 remains unresolved; 410 means expired/deleted and is permanent. There is no separate operator recovery CLI. Unknown Meta completion cannot be assumed retrievable or refunded.

Support is one Unix host with reliable local filesystem locks, SQLite and the pinned Python runtime. Windows, shared/network filesystems and multiple application hosts are unsupported. PDF admission is bounded to 50 pages/50 MiB, with separate renderer, archive and provider limits. Current live policy uses a one-hour run deadline, 100 provider attempts across the document retry chain, and a per-document cap no greater than $30 within the authorized shared allowance.

## Reading-guide configuration

The `amuseme-meta-3` configuration uses Muse Spark 1.3 at high effort with prompt version `amuseme-1`, a bounded JSON response, and a $0.50 worst-case reservation for the guide stage (it was $1.50 before the November 2 cost model below). The shared allowance follows the explicit authorization below; all prior charges remain counted. Mandatory preflight includes this reservation before extraction. Historical configurations omit both the guide model and its optional reservation and skip the guide step locally; a guide dispatch without either setting fails before a paid call. Step behavior is in the [reading-guide rules](../step-rules/reading-guide.md).

## Processing allowance

Current cumulative ceiling: **$360.564373**, budget ID unchanged, $30 per document. Each raise below was explicitly authorized by the user; all prior charges remain counted. Ceilings are worst-case reservations, not measured provider bills. Disable processing after each authorized batch; a failed run does not authorize unbounded retries or extra documents.

### November 1 reading-guide acceptance allowance

The user explicitly authorized up to $30 for one fresh six-page upload-to-download test. Immediately before that test, the preserved original budget identity contained 129 charges accounting for $70.564373 (actual cost when known, otherwise the full reservation). The new cumulative configuration ceiling is therefore $100.564373, leaving at most $30 of new accounted work. This is a reservation ceiling, not a measured provider bill or forgiveness of earlier charges. Keep the same budget ID and every ledger row; do not reset reservations. The per-document cap remains $30. Disable processing after this one acceptance run; a failed run does not authorize unbounded retries or a second paper.

### November 2 additional-papers allowance

The user explicitly authorized up to $60 more to process two additional short papers: one with data tables and one with plotted figures. The cumulative configuration ceiling is therefore $160.564373 with the same budget ID and every prior ledger row. The per-document cap remains $30. Choose papers whose mandatory reservations fit that cap. Disable processing after the two runs; a failed run does not authorize unbounded retries or a third paper.

### November 2 document-types allowance

After the two additional papers, the user explicitly authorized up to $100 more to process four short documents of other types: a biomedical article, a legal opinion, a class handout and a business or economics brief. The cumulative configuration ceiling is therefore $260.564373 with the same budget ID and every prior ledger row. The per-document cap remains $30. Disable processing after these runs; a failed run does not authorize unbounded retries or a fifth document.

### November 2 Muse review allowance

Three of the four document-type runs failed on rejected model answers before Muse review existed, consuming reservations. After Muse review steps were added, the user explicitly authorized raising the reservation ceiling by $100 to $360.564373 so the remaining documents could finish, including review rounds. Same budget ID and ledger; the per-document cap remains $30. Disable processing after these runs.

## Meta-only runtime transition

New normal uploads use extraction prompt version 2 with one guarded Spark request per physical page. Source-page figure regions retain explicit hashes, integer pixel bounds and a rendering recipe. Assets without provenance remain historical unspecified assets. Published old revisions stay readable; old non-Meta runs cannot dispatch or retry in this runtime. Do not relabel stored configurations or rewrite receipts to migrate them. Preserve the original ledger and policy records. A changed configured policy can intentionally make historical retries fail closed.

Before extraction, mandatory reservations for extraction, page checks, headings and the reading guide must fit the saved document cap. Figure count is unknown before extraction, so figures are not in this check.

**Cost model (November 2).** Every Meta call is preflighted with Meta's free token count. The guard rejects a call before any paid work when its worst-case charge exceeds its reservation. The worst case is the counted input plus the 65,536-token framing reserve, all at the uncached $1.25 per million input rate, plus the full 16,384-token output ceiling at $4.25 per million. The output ceiling alone costs $0.0696, and reasoning tokens count toward it. The rates are `metaRates` in the [processing policy](../../src/processing/config.ts). Because a call can no longer cost more than its reservation, reservations are set from observed usage with wide headroom, not from the 524,288-token context ceiling:

| Reservation | Before | Now | Largest admitted input | Largest observed input / output |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| extraction (per page) | $2.50 | $0.30 | 118,758 tokens | 4,785 / 8,270 |
| page check (per page and per review round) | $1.50 | $0.30 | 118,758 tokens | 9,693 / 12,896 |
| headings | $1.50 | $0.50 | 278,758 tokens | 11,090 / 3,180 |
| guide | $1.50 | $0.50 | 278,758 tokens | 15,347 / 11,484 |
| figure description | $1.50 | $0.50 | 278,758 tokens | 6,506 / 1,647 |
| figure crop review (new `figure-crop` key) | $1.50 (figures) | $0.20 | 38,758 tokens | not yet run live; two images and a short JSON prompt, about 10,000 tokens |

The observed figures come from all 111 completed calls in the November 1–2 ledger. The most expensive call cost about $0.064 at the published rates, and the average was $0.012–$0.047 depending on stage. Headings, guide and figure descriptions read the whole document, so their reservation covers about twice the text of a 50-page upload.

Mandatory preflight is now $0.60 per page plus $1.00, so up to 48 pages fit the $30 cap; PDF admission still stops at 50 pages. Each figure can cost up to $0.90 more: two crop-review rounds and one description. A 15-page document with 5 figures reserves at most $14.50, which leaves $15.50 for Muse review rounds of $0.20–$0.50 each. With 5 figures fully reviewed, up to 40 pages fit before review rounds.

Crop reviews and Muse reviews are admitted only when they fit beside every charge, every outstanding reservation and the remaining mandatory reservations. When the budget is short, a crop stays unreviewed with a located warning and a review falls back safely. A call whose counted input exceeds its reservation fails as `limit-exceeded` before any paid call. In a review or crop round, it falls back the same way.

Missing actual charges still retain the full reservation, so the ledger counts each new call at $0.20–$0.50 instead of $1.50–$2.50. Documents bound to the earlier policy keep it, and retries or validator repairs against that policy fail closed under the new one. Historical configurations without a guide keep their four-stage provider policy, with no guide reservation or dispatch. Per-call checks also enforce the remaining global budget, so this minimum is not a promise that a run is funded. The October 28 explicit $30 addition set the earlier allowance to $70 ($3 setup/$67 processing); the separately authorized November 1 acceptance allowance above supersedes its configuration ceiling. All prior charges remain counted. Existing documents keep their original caps and policies. The historical version-1 CLI keeps its original $37 ceiling; use the normal upload workflow for the separately authorized full-document test.

The experimental [Spark extraction CLI](../../cli/spark-extraction/README.md) is included in normal TypeScript and lint checks. Focused offline coverage is `pnpm exec vitest run tests/paper/spark-extraction.test.ts tests/processing/spark-trial.test.ts tests/processing/pipeline.test.ts`. Its default inspection mode makes no provider calls; `--run` is a separate authorized live action against the original ledger. See the [single-page result](../research/spark-extraction-trial-2026-10-28.md) for observed fidelity, exact artifacts and the remaining allowance. Normal uploads now use serial version-2 Meta extraction, with blank-page retention and provenance-labeled figure regions. The historical single-page live result does not establish multipage/table/figure quality. Offline integrated coverage includes `tests/processing/meta-document.test.ts`; current runtime checks use no live data.

The [submission reconstruction utility](../step-rules/submission-preparation.md) has a separate offline check: `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests/submission -v`. Reconstruct the selected tree from its hash-pinned foundation before running the application checks below. Keep the foundation outside the submitted repository.

Exercise the affected behavior in a real browser. Use Chrome through supported CUA accessibility/native controls or Chrome DevTools when one attaches to a usable window. The Chrome extension can be disconnected, CUA keypresses may not reach automation-controlled Chrome, and Chrome started with `--remote-debugging-pipe` exposes no attachable port. Otherwise use the cmux built-in browser as described in [browser verification](../../.agents/skills/browser-verify/SKILL.md). cmux is WebKit (the Safari engine), so record the engine with every result and do not report it as Chrome evidence. Chrome-only behavior, such as native downloads, still requires Chrome. Playwright runners have been retired; do not use Playwright or `cmux browser repl`. Confirm the actual serving checkout, build, URL, and browser window before recording results.

Never launch Chrome from a shell command. If Chrome crashes or fails to launch, do not relaunch it; inspect existing logs. If no supported driver works, stop browser testing and report the blocker. Do not change browser security policy or bypass an authorization rejection. Close every tab or surface you opened and report anything left open.

`pnpm dev` builds and watches the guarded server; `pnpm dev:app` watches UI builds. `pnpm build` creates the app, stock Studio, and `dist/server.mjs`; `pnpm start` serves that production bundle. The running server serves the UI from `.mastra/output/app`; only `pnpm build` updates it, not `pnpm build:app` alone.

A server started with `node --env-file=<file> --watch src/server/main.ts` restarts when any file in its import graph changes (`src/domain`, `src/server`, `src/storage`, `src/processing`, `src/paper`, `src/mastra`). A restart kills an in-flight paid run, so do not edit those paths during one; `src/app/` and docs are safe. A watch restart does not re-read `--env-file`: after changing the env file, stop the process and start it again. See [live paid run](../../.agents/skills/live-paid-run/SKILL.md). Use the guarded entry point. Follow the [joint Mastra/Studio upgrade procedure](mastra-upgrade.md) for dependency changes.

## Hackathon publication boundary

The public `timezyme/meta-hackathon-paper-tours` repository contains only the event submission's changes and reconstruction files. Its Git history is intentionally independent of this full working checkout. Do not push this checkout's inherited history to that repository. Reconstruct the app using the separately published, hash-pinned `timezyme/amuseme-foundation` archive and the public README; keep its licensing grant and third-party notices with the source. The local application's original data directory and budget ledger are never publication inputs.

Complete direct Chrome verification on the frozen candidate using the [development harness](development-harness.md#verify-in-a-browser). Inspect registered agents, workflow graph/run details and traces in stock Studio, plus ordinary-user/anonymous denial and direct API restrictions. Exercise reader, downloads/copy, ratings, retries, deletion and reconnect. Record errors, versions, command results, artifact hashes and serving URL. Any live-provider check retains its separate authorization.

Current upload disclosure identifies Meta page extraction/checking and text/figure processing. Reader attempt details show the nested extraction model configuration and its available versioned public prompt. Historical extraction receipts without a model retain their saved provider/version display. The immutable version-1 extraction prompt stays in its historical backend module; its public UI template remains unavailable.

The reader calls exported images “source images.” They may be crops of rendered pages; the interface must not imply they are the PDF's native embedded images.

The browser provides sign-in, the authenticated AmuseMe upload/dashboard, processing states, and the saved-output reader. The server owns session validity, roles, document authorization, admission, and processing.

3. Browser session state is checking, signed out, authenticated, or unavailable. Pathname changes and returning to a visible tab recheck the session; document-query changes retain the authenticated session and loaded output. Sign-in query changes still resolve the complete return path. Expired sessions show sign-in, preserving only `/` or a valid `/documents/:documentId` with bounded document-view parameters: page, mode, selected goal, step/claim number, paper-map node number, source number and source/reader view. Reject duplicate or unknown parameters, encoded values, external URLs, protocol-relative URLs, encoded separators and unknown paths. Never put document text or quotations in URLs or browser storage.

5. Use the application’s local logo and matching favicon in `src/app/assets/`. Keep the same symbol geometry across the light and dark wordmarks and favicon. Preserve the Geist font and license, spacing, olive palette, dark default, and light alternative. Prototype previews mirror these brand assets. Persist only the theme in localStorage. A denied storage operation leaves the chosen theme usable for the visit and reports that persistence failed. Local storage never contains credentials or sessions.
6. Form labels, autocomplete, native email validation, visible focus, pending status, and associated error text are required. Error and session messages use live regions. Layout must fit 320, 390, 1024, and desktop widths in both themes without horizontal overflow. History Back/Forward must preserve route behavior. Sign-in input boundaries have at least 3:1 contrast in both themes, and mobile input text is at least 1rem. A ready route owner sets the page title and focuses its main landmark once per pathname transition, including history navigation through loading routes; checking/loading placeholders, query changes and background refreshes do not consume that focus request.

The library opens with a one-sentence statement of what AmuseMe does, the tagline and three numbered steps, then upload (when enabled) above the saved documents. It features one saved paper with its first page and title, and a guided paper offers a direct link to its first cited passage. Show guide links and counts only after validating the saved guide and its receipt. A paper without a guide opens in the full reader. Keep pending runs, upload admission, download options and deletion reachable. When uploads are disabled, keep saved papers available.

After confirmed upload admission, navigate to its document. While queued/running, show actual saved progress beside goal selection (first on phones): a plain sentence from the saved stage and units ("Muse is checking page 2 of 4"), the ordered list of configured stages marked done, in progress or up next, and the time elapsed since the run's saved `startedAt`. No invented timers, estimates of remaining time or percentages; the only duration copy is the fixed note that a short document usually takes about five minutes. A `limit-exceeded` run failure or upload refusal reads as a friendly too-long message that suggests a shorter PDF or excerpt; other failures keep the server's message. Readers may choose a walkthrough or claims while waiting, or open the exact original PDF immediately. Keep the selected goal/page in bounded URL state through publication. Guide buttons become available only after validated saved output arrives. Failures retain original access and expose only server-authorized explicit retries.

3. Use compact `JSON.stringify` bytes for the three JSON documents, matching OutputStore's checked serialization. Hash the exact returned UTF-8/image bytes through Effect Crypto. Image bytes must match the canonical image path/type/count/hash; reject missing, extra, duplicate, or conflicting files. No image transformations or network calls occur during export. Preserve rendered-region provenance in document.json and images.json and identify it in normalized.txt. Historical assets without provenance remain unspecified.

Covers: route:POST:/api/documents, route:GET:/api/documents, route:GET:/api/documents/:documentId, route:GET:/api/documents/:documentId/status, route:GET:/api/documents/:documentId/original, route:GET:/api/documents/:documentId/preview, route:DELETE:/api/documents/:documentId, route:POST:/api/documents/:documentId/retry

The preview route requires a valid `page` query within the document and returns a PNG rendered from that original page using the bounded existing PDF renderer. It renders the stored original in place after the same owner and expiry checks as original download; the renderer verifies its size, hash and private ownership, and access is rechecked after rendering. One preview render may run at a time; a competing request gets 429. A scoped private `preview-` directory holds only the rendered page and is removed on success, failure or cancellation; preview rendering has a 20-second deadline and makes no model calls. Keep no-store and frame denial. The original download remains unchanged. UI failures show an explicit retry and original-download link.

1. Render only the owner-authorized current output revision. Decode canonical document, processing report, and rating with shared product schemas and reject mismatched document/revision/run identities. Keep queued, failed, interrupted, loading, expired, unauthorized, and unreadable output states explicit. There is no fixture fallback in application code. Preserve typed HTTP status in both document and output read errors: 410 offers return/re-upload guidance without retry; ambiguous 404 and temporary failures retain explicit retry.
2. The goal-first workspace offers a saved overview, one walkthrough step or claim per screen, completion and return to choices. It retains the Live Page reading surface, page/section sidebar, prominent Copy and ZIP actions, and Downloads & details in a native modal dialog at every width. Historical output without a guide explains its absence and retains the full reader/downloads. Preserve the brand, serif document body, dark default/light theme, complete report, rating and deletion controls. Under 900px the source sidebar becomes a Pages modal. The Original/Clean copy switch preserves the selected source page; preview uses an authenticated image of that single original page without inference. The original remains downloadable when preview rendering is unavailable. Use actual report issues and warn that AI output may be wrong; do not carry sample-specific edit counts, explanations or source boxes into real documents.

4. Render text-format blocks literally with preserved newlines/whitespace and wrapping; never infer Markdown or code from their content. Canonical heading kind/level controls heading markup and removes its normalized heading prefix. Other declared formats retain Markdown/GFM, sanitized HTML tables and intentional math through public renderer packages. Sanitize before trusted KaTeX rendering and disable trust features. Uploaded HTML cannot supply scripts, styles, active controls, unsafe links, or image loads. Only canonical figures use the owner-authorized image route. Literal newlines and HTML breaks inside table cells remain visible. Wide tables/equations scroll inside the reader; they cannot widen the viewport. Prose and list children have a 52ch reading measure while figures, tables and equations retain the available width.

6. Display report counts directly, retaining unavailable metrics as unavailable. Summarize saved Muse reviews in plain words: a corrected review says the check caught and fixed a problem; a fallback says Muse checked it and kept the original text (or headings, or published without a figure description or guide). Issues backed by a recorded fallback lead with that sentence and link to compare the page. Disclose actual receipt model, effort, prompt name/version, attempt state, delivery, and reported usage/cost. Public prompt templates are selected only by an approved exact version mapping. Never expose raw provider replies, hidden reasoning, credentials, or fabricated quality scores. The download summary states the unresolved issue count and offers Review issue(s), which opens and focuses that panel instance’s native report summary. Rating buttons retain their visible names.

10. Guide evidence resolves quotations only against immutable source blocks. Display the exact quotation highlighted within its actual stored source block, with other source blocks from that page and an Original switch. Source locations supply page choices; page-only locations never acquire invented pixel boxes. Guide text renders as literal text. Read boundaries reject invalid citations or a guide without its matching accepted completed receipt. Bounded URL state restores modes, steps, claims, source selection and view on refresh/history; explicit guide turns focus the new heading without status polls stealing focus. Arrow shortcuts apply only outside interactive controls and open dialogs.

Extraction freezes page and block IDs. Public page numbers start at one. A page records rendered dimensions, source dimensions, source origin, rotation, DPI, and the affine transform from source units to rendered pixels. The transform is `x' = a*x + c*y + e`, `y' = b*x + d*y + f`. Boxes use top-left rendered pixels. Missing boxes use page-only locations. Assembly keeps all original source blocks and all locations contributed by joined blocks. References, notes, tables, captions, equations, lists, code, and unclassified content remain explicit. Code is a supported block kind; its literal content, declared format and source locations survive extraction, assembly and export. Historical unclassified source blocks are not relabeled on read. Native table markup is content, not permission to execute HTML.

Figure identity, asset availability, author caption, and generated description are independent. New Meta figures identify their rendered source-page region, PDF hash, verified PNG hash and dimensions, integer crop recipe and actual output dimensions. Optional provenance preserves historical unspecified metadata; its absence is no proof of native origin. Missing descriptions leave figures intact and require a located warning before successful publication. Source blocks remain available for reader and export accounting.

Provider receipts start before dispatch. Prepared receipts contain no provider-assigned ID. Completed receipts identify the saved response and its validation result. Unknown completion remains a distinct state. Extraction receipts retain provider/version and, for Meta extraction, the actual nested model configuration. New Meta extraction checkpoints cover every physical page with distinct accepted receipts in page order. Receipt page and figure IDs identify the processed unit. Failed runs retain stage and unit context.

5. Reservations use integer micro-US dollars, including configured OCR costs. Admission checks known actual charges plus every outstanding reservation against both the run cap and the named authorized budget. The independent charge ledger survives document deletion without retaining document payloads. Missing actual charges retain the full reservation even after success. Unknown completion retains its reservation. Only a proven undispatched attempt or a reported actual charge can reduce the reservation. A new budget identity requires a new authorized allowance. The current explicit acceptance allowance is recorded in the [operations runbook](../runbooks/application-operations.md#november-1-reading-guide-acceptance-allowance); the per-document cap remains $30, bounded by the configured processing total. Preserve stage reservations, the original budget ID, historical policies and all charges; configuration does not reset remaining allowance.

7. Live processing requires explicitly enabled access, the Meta credential, a positive authorized spending cap and positive worst-case stage charges. MinerU configuration is optional historical cleanup metadata. Offline fixtures require an explicitly injected fixture policy. Missing live configuration fails before provider work; the HTTP admission layer must expose the same availability result.
8. The guard owns paid retries. There are no automatic paid retries. Browser mutations, Mastra step retries, model SDK retries, transport retries and remote job submission retries remain zero. A fresh attempt requires an owner-authorized request persisted with its new run and exact attempt grant, plus acknowledgment of possible repeated work when completion is unknown. Caller strings grant nothing. Complete transient Meta responses may receive an explicit bounded retry; invalid output cannot. Invalid output instead gets at most two [Muse review](muse-review.md) attempts with the `review` tag: each references a completed answer for the same unit, counts toward the unit's attempt allowance, and keeps the remaining mandatory reservations free. `ProviderGuard.rejected` returns the saved rejected answer for an exact request so resumed and retried runs replay it. A retry grant applies only to its exact request fingerprint; a unit's other completed requests keep replaying. Retry requests skip completed rejected answers rather than resending them. Each new attempt reserves its own budget, with earlier charges and uncertain reservations counted across the unchanged document policy. A still-live prior attempt cannot be retried concurrently. Existing MinerU UUIDs recover through GET, never another POST. See [run recovery](run-recovery.md).

12. The optional guide model and worst-case reservation preserve old stored configurations and policies. A guide dispatch requires both explicitly; never choose another stage's configuration or default an absent reservation to zero. New normal uploads configure the guide and account for it in mandatory preflight. For historical configurations without a guide, binding, retry and validator repair compare the current policy with only the new guide reservation omitted. Every other field still must match exactly. This projection does not rewrite the saved policy or ledger and cannot raise an earlier allowance.
13. A unit is `{stage, pageIds, figureId}` plus an optional `task`. Only figure crop review sets it (`figure-crop`); the task joins the unit key, receipt and fingerprint only when present, so existing keys and fingerprints are unchanged. A first attempt may carry `headroomMicrousd`: like a review, it is admitted only when its reservation fits beside every charge, outstanding reservation and that headroom, so discovered work cannot use the reservation of remaining mandatory stages.
14. Each Meta call's reservation must cover its worst-case charge. Before preparing an attempt, the pipeline prices the counted input plus the framing reserve at the uncached input rate and the full output ceiling at the output rate, using the policy's `metaRates`. If that exceeds the stage reservation, the call fails `limit-exceeded` before any attempt row or charge. Figure crop review reserves the optional `figure-crop` amount; a policy without it uses the figures reservation. Guard admission and validator repair choose this reservation by stage and task. Policies without `metaRates` (historical and offline fixtures) skip the price check and keep their flat reservations.

1. Input is the full corrected document, the original Figure and its verified image bytes. Retain its original caption, source IDs, locations, and image link. Historical assets retain their saved metadata. New Meta assets are explicit rendered-page regions with host-verified bytes and provenance, not native embedded images. Never silently substitute a full page or a caption for the selected figure.

4. Missing/unavailable image assets produce no request. Preserve the original figure with unavailable description and a located `figure-description-unavailable` issue. Keep the converter's separate `figure-asset-unavailable` issue: publication requires both when both are missing. A failed description similarly remains an unavailable figure rather than disappearing.
